The structure in question is a single-story, wood- framed garage approximately 8 feet by 16 feet (128 square feet) in footprint. The building is situated on the property line, within the current code-required setbacks, and predates modern zoning and building code standards. The garage is in an advanced state of disrepair and poses a potential safety hazard. It exhibits significant structural deterioration, including: • Extensive dry rot in framing members and wall sheathing • A compromised roof structure that is sagging and unstable • Active termite or pest damage • No longer structurally sound and at imminent risk of collapse Due to the degree of degradation, the structure is considered beyond reasonable repair or mitigation. The cost of rehabilitation far exceeds the value of the structure, and its location within current setbacks makes reconstruction in the same location non-compliant with existing County codes. There is no intention to rebuild or replace the garage at this time. The proposed demolition will improve safety on the property, eliminate blight, and allow for better long-term site management and use. All demolition activities will comply with applicable Sonoma County environmental and safety regulations, including: • Proper waste disposal and material recycling • Dust and debris control measures during demolition • Compliance with erosion and sediment control if required • Disconnection and capping of any utilities serving the structure • We respectfully request approval of this demolition based on the urgent need to remove a hazardous, non-code-conforming structure that is no longer viable.
